The Yellow Subway Line (2016)

The Yellow Subway Line is a reimagining of the iconic Yellow Submarine. Picture John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr boarding the Q train on their way to the Ed Sullivan Theatre. The Blue Meanie, now a mischievous train conductor, derails the subway into a vibrant rainbow just below 54th Street. In the same car, Eleanor Rigby sits among a group of lonely souls. As the train rockets upwards, it bursts above the 13th floor of the Sullivan Theatre, where Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds casts her kaleidoscope eyes onto the moving car, bathing it in dazzling light. Suddenly, the passengers begin to embrace one another joyfully, and as liquid instruments flow into the laps of the Beatles, live music erupts. The once-muted crowd transforms, cheering and singing along to the vibrant soundscape.

“In the town with lights afar
Lived a man who rode the R
And he told us of his life
In the land of subway lines
So we third-railed on to the sun
'Til we found a G of green (G of green!)
And we lived beneath the grime
In our yellow subway line”

products.title: Syd Barrett vs. Sid Vicious post card
products.body_html:
My artwork here features an imaginative and playful boxing match poster between two iconic and wildly different figures from music history: Syd Barrett, co-founder of Pink Floyd, and Sid Vicious, the infamous bassist of the Sex Pistols. The bright yellow background and bold, chaotic typography create an eye-catching, punk-rock-inspired aesthetic that echoes the rebellious energy both musicians embodied.

Syd Barrett is depicted on the left, labeled “The Mad Cap”, a reference to his solo work “The Madcap Laughs”. He’s illustrated in boxing gear, but with psychedelic imagery swirling around him, including a striking octopus, representing the mind-altering nature of his music and the influence of LSD (referenced by the word “Acid” near his name).

Sid Vicious, on the right, is called “The Mad Punk”, with his anarchic persona fully on display. He’s depicted in a punk getup, complete with his iconic spiked hair, and the word “Anarchy” scrawled near his name, referencing his band’s hit “Anarchy in the UK”. His stance, with tattoos and visible wounds, reflects his raw and reckless nature.

The poster includes their physical stats (height, weight, reach), adding a humorous touch of realism to this fictional showdown. The date, December 17, 1978, suggests this dream bout takes place during a key era in both the psychedelic rock and punk movements, while the venue in Cambridge adds a playful reference to Barrett’s hometown.

Overall, this piece is a dynamic and witty blend of music history, pop culture, and combat sports, presenting these two vastly different yet equally influential figures as larger-than-life opponents in a surreal and chaotic match-up.

products.title: 20,000 Leagues Under NYC post card
products.body_html:
In the late 1800s, Jules Verne was inspired by a conceptual submarine model at The World's Fair in Paris, France. This inspired the creation of his novel Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea. In the story, the U.S. government assembles an expedition in New York City to hunt a mysterious sea monster using the electric Nautilus L train submarine. The narrative reaches a climax when the Nautilus encounters a school of giant squid in the Atlantic Ocean, a scene that has become iconic in literature and film.

Nearly a century later, both Verne’s novel and a Disney adaptation left a lasting impact on pop culture, inspiring countless artistic interpretations. One such interpretation emerged when I moved to New York City and spent time selling his work in subway stations. On a stormy night aboard the L train from Manhattan to Brooklyn, as the subway car rocked violently beneath the East River, I was struck by the idea of merging Verne’s classic tale with the modern New York City subway system. Imagining a submerged subway network powered by an innovative submarine system, I envisioned the L train-submarine battling a giant squid as it emerged into the East River. This creative fusion of past and present, born from a moment of inspiration, allowed me to bring a unique artistic concept to life. Only New York could’ve inspired this.

products.title: Disney vs. DeSantis post card
products.body_html:
In one corner, Ron DeSantis steps into the ring, draped in red, white, and blue, his eyes focused and determined. He’s a fighter who’s built his reputation on power moves and bold statements, ready to take on the heavyweight of entertainment. The crowd buzzes with anticipation, knowing this bout is as much about politics as it is about punches.

In the opposite corner, Disney emerges, not as a single fighter, but as a larger-than-life entity—a cultural juggernaut with decades of experience in winning over the masses. Its gloves are adorned with Mickey Mouse ears, but don’t be fooled; behind the friendly facade lies a seasoned opponent who’s been in the ring with bigger challenges and come out on top.

The bell rings, and the match begins. DeSantis comes out swinging with heavy jabs, aiming for the body, trying to weaken Disney’s foundation. His punches are driven by policy and law, targeting the core of Disney’s influence in Florida. But Disney, with its nimble footwork, ducks and weaves, countering with a flurry of its own—media blitzes, cultural influence, and public opinion, all landing sharp, precise blows.

Round after round, the fight intensifies. DeSantis throws powerful hooks, backed by legislative support, aiming to land a knockout punch. Yet Disney’s defense is strong, absorbing the hits and retaliating with creativity and nostalgia, reminding the world of its deep roots in American culture. The crowd watches, enthralled, as the battle becomes a clash of titans—one man versus a corporate empire.

The final round sees both fighters exhausted but unyielding. DeSantis delivers a strong uppercut, a decisive move that could shift the momentum. But Disney, ever resilient, counters with a combination that dazzles the audience, a reminder that its magic is hard to beat. As the bell rings to end the match, neither side has fallen, but both have taken their hits.

The fight, it seems, is far from over. The audience knows that this bout will continue beyond the ring, in boardrooms, courtrooms, and the court of public opinion. For now, the crowd is left to wonder—who truly won this round, and what will the next round bring?

My poster (or post card) is designed in a vintage fight-promotion style, with bold red and yellow typography, reminiscent of old-school boxing match advertisements.

The headdress is brightly colored with shades of purple and pink feathers, which contribute to the psychedelic feel, along with a circle framing the figure. The bold, stylized “Deadskins” text at the bottom combines the names of both influences. This mashup recontextualizes both the Grateful Dead’s countercultural aesthetic and the Redskins’ controversial history, playing with themes of legacy and cultural symbols in a visually striking way.

The combination of a skeleton, vibrant colors, and the mix of styles gives the piece a rebellious and irreverent tone, harkening back to both Redskins and Grateful Dead.

products.title: Ver Mouth post card
products.body_html:
“Ver Mouth” is a clever and playful homage to the classic French vermouth, infused with an Art Nouveau aesthetic. In this piece, the wordplay shifts Vermouth to Ver Mouth, highlighting the character’s exaggerated mouth as the focal point. The figure is a glamorous woman, drawn with elegant, fluid lines typical of the Art Nouveau style, characterized by her sweeping pose and flowing attire. The hat, feathered gown, and poised demeanor give off an air of sophistication, while her oversized lips and the play on words inject a sense of humor into the scene.

She holds a small glass of vermouth, balancing it gracefully, further reinforcing the connection to the drink, but the witty title and her smug, confident expression add a layer of lightheartedness. The use of minimal colors, with striking red lips and a white dress against a black background, allows the viewer to focus on the whimsical nature of the character.

This piece draws from the elegant, ornate style of early 20th-century French advertising posters, while reimagining it with a modern, cheeky twist that combines nostalgia and humor.

products.title: Union Square Space Station post card
products.body_html:
“Union Square Space Station” reimagines the iconic New York City subway hub as a futuristic space station, blending urban transportation with space exploration. The central structure, labeled “Union Square,” serves as the core of the station, towering above a circular design that mimics the layout of a space station orbiting in the vast expanse of outer space. The piece retains familiar elements of the Union Square subway station, with platforms designated for the N, Q, and 6 lines, which now act as futuristic docking bays for intergalactic travel.

 The design is sleek and high-tech, with a cylindrical structure that’s reminiscent of a spaceport or control tower, while still maintaining the recognizable features of New York’s transit system. The piece humorously predicts a future where urban hubs like Union Square expand beyond Earth, functioning as key waypoints in a galaxy-wide network. The American flag on the station suggests that this Union Square is part of a broader vision of space colonization.

 This artwork plays with the intersection of everyday life and science fiction, making the familiar subway setting feel grand and otherworldly. It’s both imaginative and detailed, evoking a future where the infrastructure we know today evolves into something fit for space travels.

This witty, playful design brings rock ‘n’ roll legends together in a dramatic and exciting visual format, reminiscent of the vibrant promotional posters of old-school boxing matches.

products.title: Elon Musk vs. Jeff Bezos post card
products.body_html:
My artwork here is a humorous and inventive fight poster that imagines a boxing match between two of the world’s most influential tech titans: Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos. Titled as a bout to take place in the International Space Station, this poster brings the rivalry between the two billionaires to the forefront in a playful and exaggerated way.

Elon Musk is referred to as “Pretoria’s Power Punch Prince of Progress” with the tagline “Einstein-Like Precision”, highlighting his South African origins and his reputation as an innovator through companies like Tesla and SpaceX. He is illustrated on the left, preparing for the fictional match. The tagline “Winner Claims Mars” humorously alludes to Musk’s real-world ambitions of colonizing the red planet.

On the right, Jeff Bezos is labeled as “KO’ing Industries” and “Houston’s Heavy Hitting Head Honcho,” referencing his success with Amazon and Blue Origin. The poster humorously emphasizes their ongoing competition in space exploration, a real-life race that has seen both billionaires competing to make advancements in space travel.

The vintage boxing poster design, complete with prices for general admission, ringside seats, and “fly me to the moon” references, evokes a 1950s style, contrasting with the futuristic space setting. This juxtaposition adds a layer of charm and satire, positioning the match as an epic battle for control of the future of space exploration.

It’s a visual representation of the larger-than-life personas of these two figures, playing off both their public images and their private ambitions. It looks like Musk has the edge!

By combining humor, nostalgia, and real-life sports drama, this piece offers a witty commentary on the personalities and tensions that define the Knicks’ saga.

products.title: A-Bombshell post card
products.body_html:
One of the all time favorite pieces I have created- titled “A-Bombshell,” is a creative fusion of two powerful symbols: Marilyn Monroe’s iconic skirt-blowing scene from The Seven Year Itch and the imagery of an atomic bomb explosion. The figure’s dress mimics both the flowing lines of Monroe’s famous pose and the mushroom cloud of an atomic blast, combining sensuality with the destructive power of nuclear energy.

The mushroom cloud emanates from the figure’s head, with the lower part of the dress billowing out, evoking both the natural motion of fabric in the wind and the chaotic, violent energy of an explosion. This clever duality plays with contrasts: beauty and destruction, glamour and chaos. The sneakers worn by the figure add a modern, grounded element to the surreal and iconic imagery above, offering a playful twist on the traditional glamor associated with Marilyn Monroe.

The monochrome color palette highlights the detailed linework, emphasizing the swirling texture of the “mushroom cloud dress” and the clean simplicity of the figure’s legs and shoes. The balance between classic Hollywood and the atomic age in “A-Bombshell” captures a moment in cultural history where both these forces were at the forefront of global consciousness. This piece not only references pop culture but also comments on the simultaneous allure and threat of power.

products.title: Gumbit, Crumb, Picasso post card
products.body_html:
Your artwork brings together several rich influences in a striking, layered way. The piece fuses elements from Robert Crumb’s textured, intricate line work with Picasso’s emotional and abstract style, particularly evoking “The Old Guitarist.” This synergy of styles is evident in the way you depict exaggerated, almost surreal expressions and textures, giving the figure a raw, emotional depth.

 

Gumbit sits playing a banjo, and the figure itself has dual faces—a visual choice that might symbolize contrasting personas or a fragmented self. One face is somber and realistic, while the other appears more exaggerated and grotesque, blending Crumb’s caricature style with the emotional weight often seen in Picasso’s figures. The fine cross-hatching and stippling techniques lend a sense of depth and shadow, while the ornamental flourish near the banjo adds an unexpected, almost whimsical touch that contrasts with the rest of the image.

 

Overall, the artwork feels like a commentary on the complexity of identity, using stylistic and symbolic contrasts to convey multiple facets of personality and artistic expression. This piece stands as a unique homage to a couple of my aesthetic inspirations.

products.title: Dr. Fauci "The Chronic 2020" post card
products.body_html:
The Chronic 2020 by Dr. Fauci brings a satirical, pandemic-themed twist to Dr. Dre’s classic The Chronic album from 1993. Known as a mixtape from the “rapper/physician” Dr. Fauci, each track blends pandemic lingo with hip-hop energy. “Ride with Me,” featuring Clorox, offers a sanitized remix of its 1993 counterpart, still carrying the original’s edge and intensity but with a cleaner spin. Other tracks like “Contact Tracing (My Steps)” reflect the intense focus on tracing COVID-19 cases in 2020. The album’s line-up promises listeners a humorous yet potent mix, dedicated to never letting a single “patient” down, as Fauci’s lyrics aim to educate and entertain with pandemic flair.

 

With tracks humorously titled around themes like social distancing, quarantine, and “Flattening the Curve,” The Chronic 2020 is a clever parody that captures the spirit of resilience and humor during an unprecedented time.
